description: UPDATE and DELETE wired through the deferred-apply write set. Inside an explicit transaction the changes are visible to the transaction itself through the read overlay, a ROLLBACK discards them so the base store is never touched, and a COMMIT applies them - including modifying or deleting rows the SAME transaction just inserted. Three staging idioms are pinned because each was silently broken by a raw storage scan that could not see buffered rows: UPDATE ... FROM a source, where a dim loader inserts into a work table and immediately join-updates it in one transaction and the buffered rows were never updated; DELETE ... USING, the same shape for removals; and MERGE, whose SOURCE read was a raw scan blind to a stage table populated in the same transaction, so the merge silently did nothing. Converted 1:1 from transaction/UpdateDeleteDeferredApplyTest (now retired); the Java built its own engine with transaction.deferredApply=true and toggled setAutoCommit, both of which the testkit backend supplies through the default engine plus an explicit BEGIN.
